name: Ramones
hook: Four kids from Queens who made rock songs short and fast on purpose, and whose London shows in July 1976 are where British punk says it learned the speed.
blurb: The Ramones came from Forest Hills in Queens and started playing in 1974, with their first CBGB show on 16 August 1974. They all took the surname Ramone, wore the same leather jackets, and played songs that were very fast and almost never longer than two and a half minutes. They signed to Sire in late 1975 after the producer Craig Leon played their demo to Seymour Stein. Their first album, 'Ramones' (April 1976), was made at Plaza Sound in about a week for about $6,400: fourteen songs in 29 minutes, none longer than 2:41. They never had a top-40 single in America and ended in 1996. Their importance on this map is their speed, not their sales: when they played London in July 1976, British bands that saw them started playing faster.

signatureTracks.title: Blitzkrieg Bop
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The first track on the first album: a chant, three chords, and done in about two minutes.

signatureTracks.title: Judy Is a Punk
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Under a minute and a half, which was the point.
